solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Permit father's game

parts.note: father is Pa, and the apostrophe-s is kept as an S
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: A permit that belongs to Dad's game, as if a licence for his hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is an official document that permits travel abroad, so the noun is a kind of permit.

clue.text: Sudden revolutionary outbreak set above southern Switzerland

indicators.note: in a down entry, above means this piece comes first

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
CH is the international code for Switzerland, from Confoederatio Helvetica

explanation.surface: A sudden uprising breaking out above the south of Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A putsch is an attempted coup, a sudden violent bid to overthrow a government.

clue.text: Reaps fresh new plant

indicators.note: fresh means made anew, so the letters of reaps are made up again

parts.note: the five letters of this word are taken as written to be rearranged
mint condition means brand new

explanation.surface: A farmer reaps a freshly sprung plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh new' looks like a pair of adjectives for the plant; one is the signal and the other a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a species of the mint family, an aromatic garden herb.

clue.text: Just beaten by top path I stepped off

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or awry, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: these words are taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone narrowly lost after stepping off the main path.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means narrowly defeated at the finishing line, as in a horse race.

clue.text: Supposed to have place in plant

indicators.note: the placing word sits in the plant word

parts.note: a reed is a waterside plant
to place is to put

explanation.surface: A worker supposed to have a position in the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory alongside 'place', but it is a growing thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means generally believed or said to be so, a synonym for supposed.

clue.text: Ostentatious display page penned by hack

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed inside it, so the page letter goes within

parts.note: to hack is to slash

explanation.surface: A showy page written up by a jobbing journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' reads as a journalist, which suits the surface, but it is the verb meaning to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a splash is to put on a showy display, so the noun names an ostentatious show.

clue.text: Moorland photograph included loch showing perfect fitness

indicators.note: the loch letter is included within the phrase

parts.note: a photograph of moorland is a picture of heath

explanation.surface: A moorland snapshot with a loch in it shows someone in fine shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The three-word phrase comes from reading the two-word clue opening as one description.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a person who looks completely healthy, the very image of wellbeing.

clue.text: With members ready for battle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having arms, that is limbs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' suggests club membership; here it means body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works for having limbs, as in long-armed, and for bearing weapons in readiness to fight.

clue.text: Amateur Harry on manoeuvres accepted zilch

indicators.note: the jumble takes in the nought, accepting it within
troops on manoeuvres move about, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: the name and the little word are taken letter for letter to be rearranged
zilch is nothing, a zero

explanation.surface: An amateur soldier called Harry on exercises who achieved nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On manoeuvres' reads as one phrase, but 'on' belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorary post is held without pay, so it is unpaid, the sense of amateur.

clue.text: In tabernacle, rich priest emerges

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the following words
the answer emerges from inside the run of letters across the words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next holds the answer

explanation.surface: A priest comes out of a richly decorated tabernacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, a broader term that includes a priest.

clue.text: Idiot wept tears about Romeo

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, that is around, the Romeo letter
read as the verb, tears rips the word wept apart and rearranges it

parts.note: the word is taken letter for letter to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fool who cried over Romeo, perhaps at the end of the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' looks like the noun for crying beside 'wept', but it is the verb to rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or foolish person, an informal synonym for idiot.

clue.text: River parasites, fellow found one in blue

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
lice are parasitic insects
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man finds lice by a river while wearing blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boys in blue' is a British phrase for the police, from their blue uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Police officers wear blue uniforms, so a constable is a person dressed in blue.

clue.text: Fish go in wooden things one makes

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
to go in is to enter

explanation.surface: A fish that slips into some wooden objects.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a craftsman who builds things out of timber, so he is the person who makes them.

clue.text: Milk producer's steering apparatus did not start

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter, as if it never got going

parts.note: a rudder steers a boat

explanation.surface: A cow's steering gear failed to start, as if she were a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The udder is the gland of a cow or goat that produces milk.

clue.text: Lecturer with antelope or reptile

parts.note: an izard is the Pyrenean chamois, a goat-antelope

explanation.surface: A lecturer brings either an antelope or a reptile to class.
explanation.walkthrough: The izard is an obscure crossword animal: the chamois of the Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: A lizard is a scaly four-legged reptile, an example of the class.

clue.text: Auditor reportedly has piece used in Chinese game

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, giving a different spelling with the same pronunciation

parts.note: an auditor checks accounts, so is a checker

explanation.surface: An auditor is said to own a piece from a Chinese board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' hints at hearing, but here it is the accounts inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese chequers is a board game played with marbles or pegs, and its counters are called chequers in British spelling.

clue.text: Each slunk over when set free

indicators.note: over suggests turning things over, upsetting the order of the letters

parts.note: the two words are taken letter for letter to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Every prisoner crept over the wall once released.
explanation.definitionFit: To unshackle is to remove fetters, so to release someone from captivity.

clue.text: Strongly expressive in a manner of speaking

definitions.meaning: first meaning: forceful and moving in expression
second meaning: read literally, having a fine way with spoken words

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' is an idiom for 'so to speak', but here it is read literally as describing someone's way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: An eloquent speaker uses fluent, persuasive language, which is both forceful expression and a skilled speaking manner.

clue.text: Young child tells fibs about understatement

indicators.note: the fibs word goes about, that is around, the little one

parts.note: fibs are small lies
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A little child tells fibs on the subject of understatement.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech that affirms by understating, such as 'not bad' for good.

clue.text: Stands out? On the contrary occupies place in protest

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the reverse of stands out, swapping each word for its opposite
second meaning: stages a protest by occupying premises

explanation.walkthrough: Stands becomes its opposite, sits, and out becomes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Protesters who stage a demonstration by occupying a building and refusing to leave are said to do this.

clue.text: Most reliable moveable feasts

indicators.note: a moveable feast shifts date, and here the letters shift order too

parts.note: the word is taken letter for letter to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Moveable feasts, like Easter, called the most reliable thing in the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moveable feasts' is a real phrase for festivals such as Easter whose date varies, which hides the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Safest is the superlative of safe, meaning most dependable or secure.

clue.text: Patient under obligation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person being treated or studied
second meaning: ... to a duty or rule

explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' looks like the adjective for calm waiting, but it is the noun for someone under treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a person undergoing medical study and an adjective for being bound by something.

clue.text: Feel sorry about address without energy

parts.note: re is Latin for concerning, used in letters

indicators.note: without means one energy letter is left out

parts.note: to address someone is to greet them

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry about giving a speech that lacked energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' suggests a speech, but it is the verb to greet.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret is to feel remorse or sorrow over something done.

clue.text: Friend not finishing rock

indicators.note: the word stops short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends

explanation.surface: A friend who never finishes, solid as a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised 'Friend' means a member of the Society of Friends, the Quakers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to shake violently, which is what the ground does in an earthquake; a quake is a tremor.

clue.text: Legislator getting in the drink had quite enough

indicators.note: the member gets in, inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician in the drink, having had plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the drink' is slang for fallen into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means sufficient or more than enough, a synonym for plenty.

clue.text: Board where, say, there are cups and saucers

parts.note: board as in bed and board means meals, a table

indicators.note: say marks a word as it is spoken, so a word pronounced the same is wanted

parts.note: the question word sounds exactly like a word for goods or crockery

explanation.surface: A board where cups and saucers are set out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableware is the collective term for crockery and cutlery, of which cups and saucers are examples.

clue.text: Magazine's content tending to go off

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what an arms magazine stores, gunpowder and charges
second meaning: likely to blow up, volatile

explanation.surface: A magazine's articles that tend to go stale or cause a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Magazine' suggests a periodical, but it is an ammunition store.
explanation.definitionFit: Explosive is both a noun for blasting material kept in a store and an adjective for something liable to detonate.

clue.text: Cargo vessel went from reservoir to river

parts.note: a reservoir is an artificial lake

explanation.surface: A cargo boat sailed from a reservoir down to a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A laker is a freight ship built to trade on the Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Deal with jury's conclusion in agreement

parts.note: to deal with a problem is to treat it

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the word jury supplies its final letter

explanation.surface: Handling the jury's verdict in a way everyone accepts.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty is a formal pact between nations, a synonym for an agreement.

clue.text: Most restless but not starting to be most catty

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

parts.note: catty means spiteful, so the most catty is the most bitchy

explanation.surface: The most restless person is still not quite the most spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Itchy can mean restless or impatient, as in itchy feet, and this is its superlative.
